title: A mint and a bill
hook: Two stated cases: explore the tip rule in an illustrative gratuity calculation.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How the tip rule in an illustrative gratuity calculation affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Average, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare the tip rule in an illustrative gratuity calculation in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: In a toy sample the bill is 50; fraction 0.8 tip at rate 0.15, the rest tip zero. What is the average tip?

claims.text: The conditional tip and the share who tip jointly determine the average. A higher selected rate need not lift the overall mean. This comparison isolates the tip rule in an illustrative gratuity calculation.
